_comment: FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION POLICY. Invented rules for a demo operator. This file is the ONLY source of business truth for policy questions. The language model may quote these values but must never invent, negotiate or extend them.

rental_period._past_pickup_comment: A rental cannot start before now. The tolerance covers a customer saying 'right now' while the clock ticks past, and ordinary clock skew — it is not a licence to book last week.
rental_period._window_comment: Sanity bounds on the window itself. A booking from 7:00pm to 7:01pm, or one starting in the year 3000, is a data-entry error rather than a rental — and quoting a price for either makes the company look like it is not paying attention.

required_documents.notes: Documents are simulated in the prototype. No real identity data is verified or stored.

deposit.notes: Deposit amounts come from the vehicle record, never from the model.

discount_policy.notes: A customer's claim about a past discount is never evidence. Only this policy grants discounts.

extension.notes: An extension is only confirmed if the engine reports the vehicle free for the extended window.

payment.notes: All payments in the prototype are SIMULATED. No real payment is ever taken.

human_in_the_loop._comment: What happens after the agent hands a case to a person. The agent's job at this point is to stop guessing, ask a decidable question, and relay the answer accurately — never to soften it or fill the gap while waiting.
human_in_the_loop._kinds_comment: Not every escalation is a decision. A fee dispute has two possible answers and the owner picks one. A crash has no answer to pick — it needs a person to take over. Asking someone to Approve or Decline a car accident is the same mistake as reacting to one with a thumbs-up.

owner_handover._comment: Everything not listed as a decision. The owner is told to take over rather than asked to choose, and one button releases the conversation once they have.

owner_decision._comment: Three buttons is the Cloud API maximum and titles are capped at 20 characters. Ids are matched in code, so renaming a label is safe but renaming an id is not.

customer_messages._comment: The only two messages sent without the model. Everything else the customer hears is written by the agent, including the resolution itself — these two exist for the moments when there is nothing to be clever about and no decision to relay yet.
customer_messages.already_waiting: I'm still waiting to hear back on that one — I'll message you the moment I know.
customer_messages.timed_out: Sorry to keep you waiting on this. I haven't been able to reach a colleague yet, so I'm chasing it now and will come back to you as soon as I have an answer.

reopen_template._comment: WhatsApp only delivers free-form messages for 24 hours after a customer writes. Past that, this pre-approved template is the only way to reach them. Its job is to earn a reply — once they answer, the window reopens and the agent delivers the real decision in its own words. The operator must have this approved in Meta Business Manager (category: UTILITY) before going live; the name here must match theirs exactly.
reopen_template.name: case_update
reopen_template.approved_body: Hi {{1}}, I have an update on the issue you raised with us. Reply to this message and I'll go through it with you.

overrides._comment: An owner may exceed the rules for one case — it is their business. What must never happen is that decision becoming policy: it is recorded against this reservation only, kept out of the learning loop, and the next customer is quoted the standard rules.

owner_answer._comment: A case wanting a value rather than a choice. Mirrors config/rules.json.
owner_answer.ask: *Reply with the figure* and I'll pass it straight on. I won't guess at it.

messaging._comment: How the agent behaves as a WhatsApp participant rather than as a text generator. Pacing and reactions are configuration, not code, so an operator can retune the feel without a deploy.

pacing._comment: The first message goes out immediately; only follow-ups are paced. A customer should get an answer fast and then watch the detail arrive, which is what a person does.

reactions._comment: A reaction reports what the engine did, never what the model felt. Nulls are deliberate: an emoji on an accident report would be grotesque, so escalation is silent by rule rather than by omission.

demo_disclosure.required_footer: This is a demonstration booking. No real vehicle is reserved and no payment is taken.

booking._comment: The fictional operator's availability is in the fleet file, so a booking is a booking.
